response.sql:
WITH rating_counts AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rented_films
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
), shares AS (
  SELECT rating, rented_films,
         rented_films * 1.0 / SUM(rented_films) OVER () AS share
  FROM rating_counts
), average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS value FROM shares
)
SELECT SUM(s.rented_films) AS combined_rented_films,
       AVG(s.share) AS average_share,
       AVG(s.share - a.value) AS average_excess_above_average_share
FROM shares s
CROSS JOIN average_share a
WHERE s.share > a.value;

assumptions.assumption: Each rental counts once as a rented film occurrence; repeated rentals of the same film are counted repeatedly. Shares and the average are calculated across rating levels represented among linked rentals, and the average share is the unweighted mean of those rating shares.
